Chapter 10

One step, scheduled

The function both players share: given a pattern, a step index and a time, schedule every hit. Sharing it is what makes “the file sounds like the studio” a property rather than a hope.

By the end of this chapter

Factor the one piece of logic two different callers need into a pure function with a narrow interface, and make an exhaustive switch fail to compile when a case is missing.

Outputs is the whole of what the function needs from its caller: where a track’s sound goes, and the decoded file for a sample track. The live engine answers with a channel strip; the offline renderer answers with a plain gain. Neither knows about the other.

Why satisfies never at the bottom of the switch

Adding an instrument to KINDS without adding a case here would play silence for it — a bug that shows up as “the new track does nothing” with no error anywhere. track.kind satisfies never in the default branch makes it a compile error instead: if any kind is left unhandled, its type is not never, and TypeScript says so at the line that needs the case. The noFallthroughCasesInSwitch flag in tsconfig.json catches the other way to get this wrong.

A melodic note is held for 80% of its step. The gap is what makes two consecutive notes sound like two notes rather than one long one; a hold of 100% would tie every run of notes together.

Checkpoint

  • You can name the two callers of scheduleStep and what each passes as Outputs.
  • You can explain what satisfies never does and reproduce the error by adding a kind.
